==English==
{{wp}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{alter|en|thang||slang|pronunciation spelling|usually used to denote a known fad or popular activity}}
* {{alter|en|thin'||informal|pronunciation spelling}}
* {{alter|en|thinge||archaic}}
* {{alter|en|thynge||obsolete}}
* {{alter|en|ting||Caribbean creoles|MLE}}

===Etymology===
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:thing|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|thing}}, from {{inh|en|ang|þing}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*þing}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*þingą}}.

Cognate with {{cog|stq|Ding|t=thing}}, {{cog|fy|ting}}, {{m|fy|ding|t=thing}}, {{cog|nl|ding|t=thing}}, {{cog|nds-de|Ding|t=thing}}, {{cog|de|Ding|t=thing}},  {{cog|da,nb,nn,sv|ting|t=thing}}, {{cog|fo|ting|t=parliament, assembly}}, {{cog|is|þing|t=congress, assembly}}, {{cog|sco|hing|t=thing}}.

The word originally meant "assembly", then came to mean a specific issue discussed at such an assembly, and ultimately came to mean most broadly "an object". Compare {{noncog|la|rēs}}, also meaning "legal matter", and same transition from {{noncog|la|causa||legal matter}} to "thing" in Romance languages. Modern use to refer to a Germanic assembly is likely influenced by cognates (from the same Proto-Germanic root) like {{cog|non|þing||thing}}, {{cog|da|ting}}, {{cog|sv|ting}}, and {{cog|goh|ding}} with this meaning.

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# That which is considered to [[exist]] as a separate [[entity]], [[object]], [[quality]] or [[concept]].
#* {{RQ:KJV|Luke|1|1|text=Forasmuch as many have taken in hand to set forth in order a declaration of those '''things''' which are most surely believed among us...}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-06-21|author=w:Oliver Burkeman
|volume=189|issue=2|page=48|magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly
|title=[http://www.theguardian.com/technology/2013/may/10/conscious-computing-twitter-facebook-google The tao of tech]
|passage=The dirty secret of the internet is that all this distraction and interruption is immensely profitable. Web companies like to boast about […], or offering services that let you […], "share the '''things''' you love with the world" and so on. But the real way to build a successful online business is to be better than your rivals at undermining people's control of their own attention.}}
# A [[word]], [[symbol]], [[sign]], or other [[referent]] that can be used to refer to any entity.
# An individual object or distinct entity.
# {{lb|en|legal}}
## Whatever can be [[own]]ed.
## [[corporeal|Corporeal]] [[object]].
# {{lb|en|in the plural}} [[possessions|Possessions]] or [[equipment]]; [[stuff]]; [[gear]].
#: {{ux|en|Hold on, let me just grab my '''things'''.}}
# {{lb|en|somewhat|_|dated|with ''the''}} The [[latest]] [[fad]] or [[fashion]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2002|author=Roger Nichols|title=The Harlequin Years: Music in Paris 1917-1929|publisher=Univ of California Press|isbn=9780520237360
|passage=After a slow start it became the '''thing''' to do; 'everyone went to see Pbi-Pbi, no one  talked of anything but Pbi-Pbi{{...}}'}}
# {{lb|en|informal}} A [[custom]] or [[practice]].
#: {{ux|en|Cheek kissing is a French '''thing'''; you get used to it after a while.}}
# {{senseid|en|genuine phenomenon}} {{lb|en|informal|with ''a''}} A genuine concept, entity or phenomenon; something that actually exists (often contrary to expectation or belief). {{defdate|from 20th c.}}
#: {{ux|en|Q: Bacon pie? Is that a '''thing'''? A: Yes, I checked into it, and it's a '''thing'''. Some people are even connoisseurs about it.}}
#* {{quote-av|en
|actor=w:Rush Limbaugh
|title=w:The Rush Limbaugh Show
|date=24 November 1993
|medium=radio
|text=Now I don't know how many of those male flight attendants are male lesbians -- you know... (Laughter) Well, it's a '''thing'''. I mean, there's a -- it's a -- there's a feminist professor down in Tampa who's discovered a male lesbian
|footer=<small>Accessed via [https://www.english-corpora.org/coca/ COCA]</small>
}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2014|author=Marianna Papastephanou; Torill Strand; Anne Pirrie|title=Philosophy as a Lived Experience
|passage=Frequent statements of the kind “'Race' is not a '''thing'''”, “'races,' put simply, do not exist”, “'race' (as each essay subtly shows) simply does not exist” aim to discredit Todorov's claim that a relapse to an ontology of race is at place {{...}}}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2019|author=w:Adam Gopnik|title=A Thousand Small Sanities|publisher=Riverrun|year_published=2019|page=88
|passage=Conservative philosophy, in other words, is, as we say now, a '''thing''' and deserves a serious listen.}}
# {{lb|en|informal}} A unit or container, usually containing consumable [[good]]s.
#: {{ux|en|Could you get me a '''thing''' of apple juice at the store?}}
#: {{ux|en|I just ate a whole '''thing''' of jelly beans.}}
#* {{quote-av|en
|date=24 March 1998
|title={{w|Geraldo (talk show)|Geraldo}}
|text=And he invited us all in there and then he kicked the girls out a little bit later and brought me in a couple '''things''' of alcohol. And just before he brought in my second bottle of alcohol{{...}}
|medium=television
|footer=<small>Accessed via [https://www.english-corpora.org/coca/ COCA]</small>
}}
#* {{quote-av|en
|year=2011
|title={{w|We Were Here (film)|We Were Here}}
|text=I remember my friend Ben saying in the old days that he would never go to Costco and buy one of those big '''things''' of toilet paper{{...}}
|time=1:19:48
|footer=<small>Accessed via [https://www.english-corpora.org/coca/ COCA]</small>
}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2011|author=Juliette Fay|title=Deep Down True: A Novel|publisher=Penguin|isbn=9781101486184
|passage=I came home and ate a whole '''thing''' of ice cream.}}
# {{lb|en|informal}} A [[problem]], [[dilemma]], or [[complicating]] [[factor]].
#: {{ux|en|The car looks cheap, but the '''thing''' is, I have doubts about its safety.}}
#: {{ux|en|That's the '''thing''': we don't know where he is.}}
# {{senseid|en|penis}} {{lb|en|slang|euphemism}} A [[penis]].
#* {{RQ:William Burroughs Naked Lunch|page=150|passage=“Oh Gertie it’s true. It’s all true. They’ve got a horrid gash instead of a thrilling '''thing'''.”}}
# {{lb|en|slang|euphemism}} A [[vulva]] or [[vagina]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1982|author={{w|Paul Radley}}|title=My Blue-Checker Corker and Me|publisher=Fontana/Collins|location=Sydney|page=65|text=‘They reckon she lets her dogs lick her '''thing'''.’}}
# A [[living]] [[being]] or [[creature]].
#: {{ux|en|you [[poor thing|poor '''thing''']]}}
#: {{ux|en|[[sweet young thing|sweet young '''thing''']]}}
#: {{ux|en|she's a funny old '''thing''', but her heart's in the right place}}
#: {{ux|en|I met a pretty blond '''thing''' at the bar}}
# {{ng|Used after a noun to refer dismissively to the situation surrounding the noun's referent.}}
#: {{ux|en|Oh yeah, I'm supposed to promote that vision '''thing'''.}}
#*: ''Don’t forget to have Gomez postpone that shooting '''thing'''.'' {{qualifier|in reference to the execution of Fernandez}}
# {{lb|en|informal|used possessively|negative polarity}} That which is favoured; personal [[preference]].
#: {{ux|en|it's not really my '''thing'''}}
#* '''2002''', {{w|Joss Whedon}} ''et al'', "Never Leave Me", ''{{w|Buffy the Vampire Slayer}}'' (TV episode):
#* '''2006''', {{w|Corbin Bleu}}, interview with ''{{w|Tigerbeat}}'' magazine:
# {{lb|en|informal|used possessively|with "do"}} One's typical routine, habits, or [[manner]].
#: {{ux|en|let me do my '''thing''';  I'm here doing my '''thing'''}}
#* '''2006''', {{w|David Lynch}}, ''Catching the Big Fish'', Tarcher 2006, "Darkness", p. 91:
# {{lb|en|chiefly|historical}} A public [[assembly]] or [[judicial]] [[council]] in a [[Germanic]] country.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1974|translator=Haraldur Bessason|author=Jón Jóhannesson|title=A History of the Old Icelandic Commonwealth: Íslendinga Saga|page=46
|passage=In accordance with Old Germanic custom men came to the '''''thing''''' fully armed, [...]}}
#*: The ''goðar'' seem both to have received payment of ''thing-fararkaup'' from those who stayed home and at the same time compensated those who went to the '''thing''', and it cannot be seen whether they had any profit from these transactions.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1988|author=Jesse L. Byock|title=Medieval Iceland: Society, Sagas, and Power|page=59
|passage=All Icelandic '''things''' were ''skap-thing'', meaning that they were governed by established procedure and met at regular legally designated intevals at predetermined meeting places.}}
# {{lb|en|informal}} A [[romantic]] [[relationship]].
#* {{quote-book
|en
|text=I can screw you in front of everyone. I don't care, we have a '''thing''' going on, you know. I love you,” she said.
|year=2020
|author=David Gomadza
|title=EVELINA: The Alpha}}
# {{lb|en|informal}} A [[romantic]] [[couple]].
#: {{ux|en|Are John and Jennifer a '''thing''' again? I thought they broke up.}}
# {{lb|en|MLE}} {{alt form|en|ting}}.
# {{lb|en|MLE}} Girl; attractive woman.
#: {{ux|en|Look at the [[nyash]] on that '''thing'''!}}
